Petition under Section 166 and 140 of M.V. Act, 1988 for grant of compensation Award
1.

The petitioner is seeking compensation in the wake of Detailed Accident Report (DAR) filed by police corresponding to the investigation carried out in case FIR No. 714/18 U/s 279/337 IPC registered at PS. S.P. Badli Industrial Area with regard to Motor Vehicular Accident which occurred on 06.09.2018 at about 7:00 pm at main Highway GT Road, Mukarba Chowk to Alipur, in front of CNG Pump, SGT Nagar, Delhi, involving motorcycle bearing registration no. DL4SCG1414 (offending vehicle) being driven by respondent no. 1 in a rash and negligent manner.

DAR filed by police, was treated as claim petition under Section 166(4) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ('MV Act').
2.
According to DAR, on 06.09.2018, the petitioner/injured alongwith his friend namely Sh. Kasim was returning to his house from Swaroop Nagar.

At about 7:00 pm, when he was crossing the road in front of GT Road, CNG Pump, SGT Nagar, Delhi, offending vehicle which was being driven by its driver at a very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, came from Mukarba Chowk side and hit him with a great force, as MACP No. 170/19; FIR No. 714/18; PS. S.P. Badli DOD: 04.05.2023 a result of which, he sustained grievous injuries.

He was immediately taken to SRHC Hospital, Narela,
Delhi where he was medically examined vide MLC No. 5011/18 and thereafter, he was shifted to Saroj Hospital, Madhuban Chowk, Delhi.
FIR No. 714/18 was registered at PS. S.P. Badli with regard to the accident.
The offending vehicle was found to be owned by respondent no. 2 and insured with respondent no. 3/National Insurance Co. Ltd during the period in question.

3. The respondents no.1 & 2 i.e. driver and registered owner have failed to file their WS despite grant of sufficient time and opportunities and consequently, their defence was struck off vide order dated 23.05.2019 passed by my Ld. Predecessor 4.

In its written statement, the respondent no. 3/insurance company has claimed that respondent no. 1 was holding a learner licence while he was driving the offending vehicle at the time of accident without supervision of any trained driver and as such, it is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner.
However, it has admitted that offending vehicle was insured with it at the time of accident.

5. From the pleadings of the parties, the following issues were framed vide order dated 23.05.2019 passed by my Ld. Predecessor:
1.

Whether the injured Sh. Rafiq suffered injuries in road traffic accident on 06.09.2018 at about 7:00 pm at Main Highway GT Road, Mukarba MACP No. 170/19; FIR No. 714/18; PS. S.P. Badli DOD: 04.05.2023 Chowk to Alipur, in front of CNG Pump, SGT Nagar, Delhi, within the jurisdiction of PS. S.P. Badli due to rashness and negligence on the part of driver Vipin Kumar, who was driving the vehicle bearing no. DL4SCG1414 owned by M/s.
Sachkand Transport and insured with National Insurance Co Ltd?

In support of his claim, the petitioner has examined one witness i.e. himself as PW1 and his evidence was closed vide order dated 02.05.2022.
On the other hand, no evidence was adduced respondent no. 1 & 2.
However, the respondent no. 3/insurance company has examined one witness i.e. R3W1 Sh. B.S. Yadav and its evidence was closed vide order dated 04.07.2022.
7. I have heard the arguments addressed by ld counsels for the parties.

My findings on the issues are as under:
8.
For the purpose of this issue, the testimony of PW1 Sh. Rafiq (injured himself) is relevant.
In his evidence by way of affidavit (Ex. PW1/A), he has deposed on the lines of averments made in the DAR.

He has relied upon the following documents:

9. During his cross examination on behalf of insurance company, he deposed that there was no zebra crossing at the spot from where he was crossing the road.
He volunteered that there was a bus stop from where people used to cross the road.
He deposed that the driver of the offending vehicle was alone at the time of accident and there was no pillion rider on the motorcycle at the time of accident.
He denied the suggestion that accident had taken place because of his own negligence.
10. It is evident from the testimony of PW1 that insurance company could not impeach his testimony through litmus test of crossexamination.
Said witness is found to have successfully withstood the test of cross examination.
Even otherwise, PW1 himself is the injured having sustained injuries due to the accident in question.
There is no reason as to why he would depose falsely against respondent no.1.
Furthermore, it is an undisputed fact that FIR No. 714/18 u/s 279/337 IPC was registered at PS. S.P. Badli with regard to accident in question.

Copy of said FIR (which is part of DAR), would show that same was registered on the statement of MACP No. 170/19; FIR No. 714/18; PS. S.P. Badli Sh. Rafiq vs Sh. Vipin Kumar on 4 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127882532/

sentences.text: The contents of said FIR would show that complainant Sh. Kasim had disclosed the same sequence of facts leading to the accident, as deposed by PW1 during the course of inquiry.
The registration number of offending vehicle to be DL4SCG1414 is also disclosed therein.
Moreover, it is an undisputed fact that FIR No. 714/18 u/s 279/337 IPC was registered at PS. S.P. Badli with regard to accident in question.
Copy of said FIR (which is part of DAR), would show that same was registered on 07.09.2018(accident being caused on 06.09.2018 at about 7:00 pm) i.e. on the date of accident itself.
Thus, FIR is shown to have been registered promptly and without any delay.
Hence, there is no possibility of any false implication of driver of offending vehicle or false involvement of the said vehicle in this case.

11. The very fact that respondent no. 1 was chargesheeted(which is part of DAR) by the police for offences punishable u/s. 279/338 IPC would further show that Investigating Agency also concluded after completion of the investigation that accident had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by its driver(respondent no.1 herein) and same also points out towards the fact that the accident in question had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by respondent no. 1.
Hence, there is no possibility of false implication of respondent no. 1 and/or false involvement of offending vehicle at the instance of petitioner herein.
MACP No. 170/19; FIR No. 714/18; PS. S.P. Badli DOD: 04.05.2023 12.

It is pertinent to note that the respondent no.1/driver of offending vehicle was the other material witness to throw light by testifying as to how and under what circumstances, the accident had taken place.
However, he has preferred not to enter into the witness box.
Thus, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against him to the effect that the accident in question had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by him.

13. Apart from above, copy of MLC (which is part of DAR) of injured prepared at SRHC Hospital,
Narela, Delhi shows that he had been removed to said hospital on 06.09.2018 at about 8:04 pm with alleged history of RTA.
On his local examination, he was found to have sustained multiple injuries as mentioned therein.
The said injuries are consistent with the injuries which are sustained in a motor vehicular accident.
Again, there is no challenge to the said document from the side of respondents including insurance company.

14. In view of the aforesaid discussion and the evidence which has come on record, it is held that the petitioner has been able to prove on the basis of pre ponderence of probabilities that he had sustained grievous injuries in road accident which took place on 06.09.2018 at about 7:00 pm at main Highway GT Road, Mukarba Chowk to Alipur, in front of CNG Pump, SGT Nagar, Delhi, due to rash and negligent driving of offending MACP No. 170/19; FIR No. 714/18; PS. S.P. Badli DOD:
04.05.2023 vehicle by respondent no. 1.
Thus, issue no. 1 is decided in favour of petitioner and against the respondents.

MEDICAL EXPENSES 16.

The petitioner has deposed in his evidence by way of affidavit(Ex. PW1/1) that after the accident,
he was taken to SRHC Hospital, Narela, Delhi, where he was medically examined vide MLC No.
5011/18 and thereafter, he was shifted to Saroj Hospital, Madhuban Chowk, Delhi, where he remained admitted from 15.09.2018 to 19.09.2018.
He further deposed that during his hospitalization in Saroj Hospital, the pulmonary Angiography Thromboembolism was done.
He further deposed that he had sustained grievous injuries including fracture of both bone on the right side and fracture of distal and other injuries all over his body.
He further deposed that he had spent more than Rs. 2,00,000/ on his treatment.
He has relied upon medical bills Ex. PW1/3(colly).

During his cross MACP No. 170/19; FIR No. 714/18; PS. S.P. Badli DOD: 04.05.2023 examination on behalf of insurance company, he deposed that he had not filed any complaint before any authority regarding loss of his some medical bills.
He denied the suggestion that he had not incurred a sum of Rs. 2 lakhs on his treatment.
17. It is relevant to note that the injured has relied upon medical bills(Ex. PW1/3 colly) to the tune of Rs. 85,733/ only.
It is quite evident that the respondents have not disputed the authenticity and genuineness of the said medical bills during the course of inquiry.
They have also not led any evidence in rebuttal so as to create any doubt on the genuineness of said bills.
Accordingly, a sum of Rs. 85,733/ is awarded to the petitioner under this head.
LOSS OF INCOME 18.
PW1 has categorically deposed in his evidence by way of affidavit(Ex PW1/A) that he was doing private job as a Motor Mechanic and earning Rs. 20,000/ per month at the time of accident.
He further deposed that he could not work for a considerable period due to the injuries suffered by him in the accident and thus, suffered loss of income.

During his cross examination on behalf of insurance company, he deposed that he had not filed any proof in respect of his working as Motor Mechanic and earning Rs. 20,000/ per month at the time of accident.
He admitted that he had not placed on record any fitness certificate regarding his fitness and to rejoin his work.
MACP No. 170/19; FIR No. 714/18; PS. S.P. Badli DOD: 04.05.2023 19.
The medical treatment record (which is part of Ex. PW1/2 colly) of petitioner/injured, would reveal that the case of petitioner was of fracture both bone right leg and fracture of distal.

Apart from the aforesaid treatment record produced by petitioner, he has failed to file any other medical treatment record in order to show the exact period upto which he had received the medical treatment.
Nevertheless, it can not be overlooked that the petitioner had sustained fracture both bone right leg and fracture of distal as mentioned above due to the accident.
Considering the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, it is presumed that he would not have been able to work atleast for a period of 2 months or so.

Apart from the bald statement made by PW1 Sh. Rafiq that he was earning Rs. 20,000/ per month, no definite evidence whatsoever has been brought on record to prove his monthly income at the time of accident in question.
Mere bald testimony of PW1 in this regard, would not suffice.
The petitioner has also failed to file his educational qualification documents.
Thus, his loss of income has to be assessed while taking the income of an unskilled person under Minimum Wages Act applicable during the period in question.
The minimum wages of an unskilled person were Rs. 14,000/ per month as on the date of accident which is 06.09.2018.
Thus, a sum of Rs. 28,000/ (Rs. 14,000/ x 2) is awarded in favour of petitioner under this head.

sentences.text: passed in appeal bearing no. MAC.APP 518/2010 decided on 05.07.12, has held as under: " It is difficult to measure the pain and suffering in terms of money which is suffered by a victim on account of serious injuries caused to him in a motor vehicle accident.

Since the compensation is required to be paid for pain and suffering an attempt must be made to award compensation which may have some objective relation with the pain and suffering underwent by the victim.

For this purpose, the Claims Tribunal and the Courts normally consider the nature of injury; the part of the body where the injuries were sustained, surgeries, if any, underwent by the victim, confinement in the hospital and the duration of treatment".
22. The petitioner has deposed in his evidence by way of affidavit(Ex PW1/A) that he had sustained grievous injuries in the accident in question.
Thus, he would have undergone great physical sufferings and mental shock on account of the accident in question.

Keeping in view the medical treatment record of petitioner available on record and the nature of injuries suffered by him, I hereby award a sum of Rs. 75,000/ towards pain and sufferings to the petitioner.

Ld. Counsel for insurance company sought to avoid the liability of insurance company to pay the compensation amount on the ground that driving licence (DL) in favour of respondent no. 1 was found to be Learner's Licence.

For the said purpose, Ld counsel heavily relied upon the testimony of R3W1 Sh. B.S. Yadav, Senior Assistant, National Insurance Co.
Ltd.

In order to appreciate the submissions made on behalf of insurance company, it would be appropriate to refer to the testimony of R3W1 who has deposed in his evidence by way of affidavit (Ex. R3W1/A) that respondent no. 1 was having learner's licence at the time of accident and the said fact has been duly mentioned in the chargesheet filed against him in the criminal case and thus,
insurance company is not liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

He further deposed that despite service of notice u/o 12 Rule 8 CPC(Ex. R3W1/2 to Ex. R3W1/4) dispatched vide postal receipts Ex. R3W1/5 to R3W1/7, the driver and registered owner failed to produce valid driving licence in favour of R1 and same shows that there was no valid driving licence in favour of respondent no. 1 as on the date of accident.
During his crossexamination on behalf of petitioner, he admitted that they had not filed the delivery report of the registered AD sent to driver and owner of the offending vehicle.
He volunteered that they had not filed the same as the same was not received by them.
He admitted that the policy of offending vehicle was valid at the time of accident.
He denied the suggestion that insurance company was liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

As is quite evident from the aforesaid discussion that the driving licence of respondent no. 1 filed alongwith DAR has been found to be Learner's Licence, as per record of Transport Authority.

Apart from the fact that the entire testimony of R3W1 has gone totally unchallanged from the side of respondents no. 1 & 2 during the course of inquiry, the said MACP No. 170/19; FIR No. 714/18; PS.
S.P. Badli DOD: 04.05.2023 respondents also failed to produce any valid and effective DL in favour of respondent no. 1 on record.
28. As per the material filed alongwith DAR, the driving licence produced by respondent no. 1 before filing of DAR was Learner's Licence issued by Transport Authority, Sector - 16, Rohini, Delhi.

Section 3 of M.V. Act clearly stipulates that no person shall drive a motor vehicle in any public place unless he or she holds an effective Driving Licence authorizing him or her to drive the vehicle.

Section 8(1) of the same Act further provides that any person who is not disqualified u/s. 4 for driving a motor vehicle and is also not disqualified for holding or obtaining a driving licence may,
subject to the provision of Section 7 apply for issuance of Learner's Licence to him/her.

Section 8(7)
of the Act empowers the Central Government to frame the rules in order to regulate the issuance of Learner's Licence.

In exercise of power conferred by said provision, Central Motor Vehicles Rules,
1989 (as amended upto date) have been enacted by the Central Government.

Rule 3(1)(b) clearly mandates that the person holding Learner's Licence, is accompanied by an Instructor holding an effective driving licence to drive the vehicle and such instructor is sitting in such a position to control or to stop the vehicle.

Not only this, Rule 3(1)(c) further requires that the letter "L" in Red on a white background, shall be painted in the front and rear portion of the vehicle or on a plate or card affixed on the front and the rear part of such vehicle.
MACP No. 170/19; FIR No. 714/18; PS. S.P. Badli DOD: 04.05.2023 29.
Now turning back to the facts of the present case.
There is no iota of evidence available on record to show that any instructor holding effective driving licence, was sitting with respondent no. 1 at the time of accident in question.
The burden to establish this fact was upon respondents no. 1 & 2, which they have failed to discharge even on the basis of preponderance of probabilities.

Moreover, the petitioner during his crossexamination by Ld. Counsel for insurance company had deposed that the driver of the offending vehicle was alone at the time of accident and there was no pillion rider on the offending vehicle at the time of accident.

Hence, I find substance in the plea raised on behalf of insurance company that for want of valid and effective DL in favour of respondent no. 1 being proved on record, it would be termed as breach in the terms and conditions of insurance policy on the part of respondents no. 1 & 2.
Thus, insurance company is entitled to recovery rights against the respondents no. 1 & 2 jointly and severally.
Issue no. 2 is decided accordingly.

Considering the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, it is presumed that he would not have been able to work atleast for a period of 2 months or so.
Apart from the bald statement made by PW1 Sh. Rafiq that he was earning Rs. 20,000/ per month, no definite evidence whatsoever has been brought on record to prove his monthly income at the time of accident in question.
Mere bald testimony of PW1 in this regard, would not suffice.
The petitioner has also failed to file his educational qualification documents.
Thus, his loss of income has to be assessed while taking the income of an unskilled person under Minimum Wages Act applicable during the period in question.
The minimum wages of an unskilled person were Rs. 14,000/ per month as on the date of accident which is 06.09.2018.
Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the matter titled as " Vinod Kumar Bitoo Vs. Roshni & Ors."
Sh. Rafiq vs Sh. Vipin Kumar on 4 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127882532/
7 27.
Rule 3(1)(b) clearly mandates that the person holding Learner's Licence, is accompanied by an Instructor holding an effective driving licence to drive the vehicle and such instructor is sitting in such a position to control or to stop the vehicle.
There is no iota of evidence available on record to show that any instructor holding effective driving licence, was sitting with respondent no. 1 at the time of accident in question.
The burden to establish this fact was upon respondents no. 1 & 2, which they have failed to discharge even on the basis of preponderance of probabilities.
Hence, I find substance in the plea raised on behalf of insurance company that for want of valid and effective DL in favour of respondent no. 1 being proved on record, it would be termed as breach in the terms and conditions of insurance policy on the part of respondents no. 1 & 2.
Thus, insurance company is entitled to recovery rights against the respondents no. 1 & 2 jointly and severally.
